question.text: A freshly prepared radioactive source of half life <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> hours <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn></math> minutes emits radiation which is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>64</mn></math> times the permissible safe level. The minimum time, after which it would be possible to work safely with source, will be _____ hours.

solution.text:
Given here, T=150 minutes,

A0=64x, where, x is the safe limit.

Using radioactive decay law relation, A=A0×2-tT, where, t is the minimum time in hours after which it would be possible to work safely with source.

Putting the values, we have 

x=64x×2-tT

∴  t=6 T=6×2.5=15 hours
